extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of bacteriology / microbiology laboratory workers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical laboratory methods and standards for cultivating, isolating, and handling bacteria in liquid and solid media, including aerobic and anaerobic techniques, plate and tube methods, and isolation strategies. Aimed at teaching correct procedure, apparatus, and precautions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inoculation of bouillon (liquid) cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for transferring culture to a tube of bouillon using a sterilised platinum loop: keep the tubes as nearly horizontal as possible without allowing the fluid in the bouillon tube to reach the cotton-wool plug; sterilise loop; remove plugs; pass loop into culture without touching sides; emulsify inoculum in bouillon; replug; sterilise loop; label with organism name and date; incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: keep tubes horizontal to avoid contamination of plug; avoid touching tube sides or medium with the loop handle; withdraw loop keeping infected side downward; sterilise loop before and after; label with organism and date. (Steps 1–11 as given.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Solid media storage formats: oblique (slanted) vs straight tubes
rubrics_metrics.description: Solid media are stored in tubes in one of two ways: oblique/slanted tube, where medium solidified in an inclined position forming an extensive surface (employed for 'streak' or 'smear' cultivations), and straight tube, where medium forms a cylindrical mass with an upper surface at right angles to axis (employed for 'stab' or 'stick' cultivations, or for 'shake' cultivations when solidified upright).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose storage format according to intended inoculation method: oblique for surface methods (streak/smear), straight for deep inoculations (stab) or shake preparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streak culture (Strichcultur)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flame plugs, sterilise platinum loop (or spatula), charge loop, pass infected loop to bottom of tube to be inoculated and draw lightly along centre of surface of medium, terminating streak near mouth; replug, sterilise loop, label and incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique emphasizes gentle, central streaking to produce a line of inoculum; avoid dragging too deeply or contaminating tube edges. Re-sterilise loop after use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smear culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceed generally as in streak culture, but rub the infected loop all over the surface of the medium, instead of restricting the inoculation to a narrow line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when a confluent surface growth is desired; contrasts with streaking which aims to separate colonies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stab culture (Stichcultur)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flame plugs, open tubes, sterilise platinum needle and charge it with inoculum; pass needle into tube until it touches centre of surface of medium then thrust deeply into substance of medium, keeping needle in axis of medium cylinder; withdraw needle, replug, sterilise needle, label and incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When gelatine surface is concave from evaporation, liquefy and reset before use; otherwise needle entry may split the gelatine due to surface tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shake culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Liquefy nutrient gelatine (or agar) by heating; inoculate liquefied medium as for bouillon; place newly planted tube upright to solidify; label and incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to distribute organisms through the medium depth; cool and solidify upright to produce desired column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Esmarch's roll cultivation (historical/obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Liquefy tubes of gelatine, prepare dilutions of inoculum, roll the tubes held almost horizontally in groove on block of ice until gelatine sets in a thin film on inner surface of tube. Agar for roll cultivation should have 1% gelatine or 1% gum arabic added before sterilisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as obsolete in modern labs (replaced by Petri dish plate cultivations), but may be examined for historical/academic knowledge. Use for producing a thin film culture on tube walls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plate culture principle and required apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: If a small number of bacteria are suspended in liquefied medium and spread in an even layer over a flat surface each organism forms a colony. Apparatus required includes tripod levelling stand, large shallow glass dish with plate glass cover, spirit level, case of sterile Petri dishes, tubes of sterile nutrient media cooled to ~42°C, tube of cultivation to plant from, platinum loop, Bunsen burner, grease pencil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medium must be cooled to specified temperature (e.g., 42°C) before inoculation to avoid killing organisms; levelling ensures uniform medium depth and colony development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pouring plates (serial dilution plating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Method for preparing poured plates from serially diluted liquefied medium: arrange leveled platform, prepare three dilutions (tubes 1–3), add loopfuls of inoculum to tubes, mix gently to avoid air bubbles, pour liquefied medium into Petri dishes forming thin layer, label with inoculum and dilution number, incubate for days as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mix with even circular arm movement or by rotating between palms; avoid jerky movements to prevent air bubbles. Plate No. 3 typically yields well-separated colonies suitable for study; Plate No.1 often too crowded and may be omitted/replaced by bouillon or sterile salt solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level the pouring surface to ensure uniform medium depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Place glass dish on levelling tripod and by means of levelling screws adjust surface of glass to the horizontal. "This leveling is an important matter since the development of a colony is to some extent proportionate to the supply of medium available for its nutrition."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to level can cause uneven colony size and growth due to varying medium depth (e.g., in sloped tube cultures colonies nearer bottom are larger).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agar plates: temperature control and rapid processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Agar must be melted in boiling water then cooled to 45°C or 42°C in a regulated water-bath before inoculation; the entire process must be carried out very rapidly or the agar will solidify before completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain correct medium temperature to avoid thermal killing of bacteria and to ensure medium remains pourable; work quickly to prevent premature setting and lumpiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gelatine surface plates: spreading technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Pour liquefied nutrient gelatine into Petri dishes and allow to solidify; invert plate and deposit a drop of inoculum on surface; use an L-shaped spreader (aluminium/platinum) sterilised by flame to smear the drop over the surface by rotatory motion; sterilise spreader between plates; label and incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series of three plates: plate 1 often yields enormous colonies, plate 2 fewer, plate 3 usually has very few scattered colonies suitable for detailed study; sterilise spreader between uses to avoid carry-over.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agar surface plates: drying before inoculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Invert solid agar plates, rest obliquely on cover and place in incubator at 60°C for 45 minutes (or 42°C for two hours) to evaporate condensation and give medium a firm dry surface before inoculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drying prevents condensation-related spread and produces a firm surface for accurate surface plating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hanging-drop cultivation (fluid and solid media)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sterilise hanging-drop slide, prepare dilutions substituting broth for liquefied gelatine, sterilise slide in alcohol and flame, place on moistened blotting paper under bell glass, smear sterile vaseline on metal cell rim, deposit a drop of diluted broth on a sterile cover-slip, invert onto cell, seal and incubate or observe microscopically. For solid media, place drops of liquefied gelatine/agar on cover-slip and seal; useful for yeasts and can mark grid on cover-slip to identify developing colonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful sterile technique required: use fire-sterilised forceps, avoid drying (bell glass rinsed with Lysol and not dried), use warm stage if necessary. For yeasts, use rectangular cell and larger cover-slip; mark squares for colony tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hanging-block culture (Hill)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare thin agar layer (~4 mm) in Petri dish, cut out ~8 mm square block containing full thickness, transfer block under side down to sterile slide, spread inoculum on upper surface, dry slightly in incubator, seal cover-slip onto block leaving overlap, invert slide and remove from block, seal edges with melted agar, place cover-slip with block onto hanging-drop slide sealed with vaseline or white wax, observe as for hanging-drop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique allows observation of colonies developing from single germs on a block of agar attached to a cover-slip; avoid air bubbles during transfer and sealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of anaerobic cultivation
rubrics_metrics.description: The principle upon which any anaerobic method depends falls under one or another headings: (a) Exclusion of air from the cultivation; (b) Exhaustion of air from the vessel by means of an air pump (cultivation in vacuo); (c) Absorption of oxygen from the air in contact with cultivation by pyrogallic acid rendered alkaline (cultivation in nitrogen atmosphere); (d) Displacement of air by indifferent gas (hydrogen) (cultivation in hydrogen atmosphere); (e) A combination of two or more of the above methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select method based on available apparatus and purity needs; many techniques combine principles for reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anaerobic culture media additives and sealing recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever possible, nutrient media used should contain easily oxidisable substances (e.g., sodium formate 0.4% or sodium sulphindigotate 0.1%) which will absorb dissolved oxygen; addition of glucose 2% favours anaerobes. Seal all joints between india-rubber stoppers and tubulures or mouths of tubes with melted paraffin; lubricate glass stoppers and taps with resin ointment or beeswax/olive oil mixture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such additions and sealing improve likelihood of achieving anaerobiosis; recommended where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method I (Hesse's Method) for anaerobiosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a deep stab culture in straight tube medium; pour a layer of sterilised oil (olive oil, vaseline, or petroleum) 1–2 cm deep upon the surface of the medium; incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple exclusion of air by an oil overlay; suitable for many anaerobic cultivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method II (cover-slip overlay for pure cultures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Liquefy medium and pour solid plate; inoculate surface at one spot; lower sterile cover-slip (or mica disc) on to inoculated surface excluding air bubbles and press down; incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only available when dealing with pure cultivations; physically excludes air over inoculated spot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method III (Roux's Physical Method: capillary sealing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare tube cultures of fluid media; aspirate some inoculated media into capillary pipettes; seal both ends of each pipette in blowpipe flame; incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sealed capillaries physically exclude air; suitable for small-scale anaerobic cultures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method IV (Roux's Biological Method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant a deep stab; pour a 1–2 cm layer of broth cultivation of a vigorous aerobe (e.g., B. aquatilis sulcatus or B. prodigiosus) upon the surface of the medium (or an equal depth of liquefied gelatine inoculated with the aerobe); incubate. The aerobe uses up oxygen, rendering lower medium anaerobic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relies on biological consumption of oxygen by an aerobic organism above the anaerobic target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method V (vacuum/exhaustion with pump)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare tube/flask cultivations, replace cotton-wool plug with india-rubber stopper perforated and fitted with glass tubing bent at right angles and constricted; connect tubing to water or air pump with Wulff's bottle containing sulphuric acid; exhaust air from culture vessel; seal glass tube at constriction in flame; incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires pump apparatus; air exhaustion then sealing yields anaerobic conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method VI (Buchner's Method using pyrogallic acid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Buchner's tube (large glass tube with rubber stopper), add pyrogallic acid tablets and dekannormal caustic soda solution, place inoculated tube inside Buchner's tube, fit stopper tightly; pyrogallic acid dissolves and absorbs oxygen slowly; restopper caustic soda bottle and incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use approx. 1 g pyrogallic acid per 100 cc vessel air capacity; tablets act as buffer to prevent damage; allows slow oxygen absorption and is convenient for many cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method VII (Wright's Method: plug treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare tube cultivation, cut off projecting cotton-wool plug and push plug into tube 2–3 cm; add ~1 cc pyrogallic acid 10% solution to plug (absorbed), then equal amount of caustic soda solution; quickly close mouth with india-rubber stopper; incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick chemical generation of oxygen-absorbing environment within tube plug; suitable for tube cultures and when speed is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method VIII (McLeod's Method for plates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use McLeod's plate base (earthenware disc) with plasticine groove; place pyrogallic acid and sodic hydroxide tablets in interior divisions, prepare surface plate culture, add water to sodic hydroxide division to activate, invert plate bottom over base and seal into plasticine groove; label and incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good for plate cultures; tablets produce oxygen-absorbing environment when activated; plasticine seal needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method IX (hydrogen displacement in Ruffer/Woodhead flask)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sterilise small flask, inoculate large quantity of medium, transfer inoculated medium to flask, insert sterilised india-rubber stopper and connect one side tube to hydrogen supply and the other to water basin; pass hydrogen until air is replaced (test gas), close clips, disconnect, incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displacement by hydrogen requires gas supply and testing of exiting gas; ensure removal of oxidising gases and correct sealing before incubation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method X (Botkin's method with bell jar and glycerine/mercury)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place cultivations on leaden cross in large dish, cover with bell jar, set U-shaped glass tubes as gas entry/exit, fill dish with glycerine or mercury to form seal, pass hydrogen through to replace air, clamp tubes and disconnect, incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when larger jars/multiple cultures are handled; use heavy fluid (glycerine/mercury) to seal U-tubes and maintain atmosphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method XI (Novy's jar with gas entry/exit and sealing handle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place cultivations in jar, lubricate stopper and insert with handle aligned to side tubes, connect entry tube to hydrogen supply and exit tube to basin to test gas; when air displaced, turn handle to seal orifices at right angles to tubes and disconnect gas apparatus; incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor escaping gas to confirm displacement before sealing; sealing mechanism preserves anaerobiosis after disconnection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method XII (Bulloch's jar — recommended reliable method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Bulloch's jar and glass slab; arrange pyrogallic acid and sodic hydroxide tablets inside, smear jar flange with resin ointment and apply to slab, connect gas supply and aspirate small volume with air pump to create slight vacuum, run water into pipette to dissolve soda and activate pyrogallic acid, reverse tubes, seal, and incubate. Noted: "This last method is the most satisfactory for anaerobic cultivations, as by its means complete anaerobiosis can be obtained with the least expenditure of time and trouble."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified steps (tablets per air capacity, water activation) and ensure all joints are tight; recommended as the most satisfactory method on this list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview: Methods of isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief methods to isolate organisms in a state of purity from mixtures are given as: A. By Mechanical Separation (surface plate cultivation, Esmarch's roll, serial cultivation), and B. By Biological Differentiation (differential media — selective/deterrent, differential incubation, differential sterilisation, differential atmosphere cultivation, animal inoculation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice depends on circumstances; a combination often gives quicker, more reliable results. Experience is the reliable guide, but surface plate and serial cultivation are generally most convenient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical separation: surface plate cultivations (gelatine, agar, serum agar, blood agar, hanging-drop/block)
rubrics_metrics.description: Surface plate cultivations on various media (gelatine, agar, serum agar, blood agar) and hanging-drop or block methods are enumerated as mechanical separation techniques for obtaining pure cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare plates as per earlier plate and surface plate procedures (pouring, drying, spreading); choose medium appropriate to organism and isolation aim (e.g., blood agar for hemolytic organisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serial cultivation (dilution and subculturing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Serial cultivation is listed as a mechanical separation method for isolation (historically dilution was used but is less reliable than modern plate methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serial dilution followed by plating or replanting can isolate organisms; combine with surface plate approaches for better reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological differentiation methods for isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Isolation can be effected by differential media (selective or deterrent), differential incubation temperatures/times, differential sterilisation, differential atmosphere cultivation, or animal inoculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose biological differentiation approaches when organisms have distinct physiological traits that can be exploited to separate them from mixtures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on selecting isolation method
rubrics_metrics.description: "The selection of the method to be employed in any specific instance will depend upon a variety of circumstances, and often a combination of two or more will ensure a quicker and more reliable result than a rigid adherence to any one method. Experience is the only reliable guide, but as a general rule the use of either the first or the third method will be found most convenient, affording as each of them does an opportunity for the simultaneous isolation of several or all of the varieties of bacteria present in a mixture."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical recommendation: prefer surface plate cultivation or serial cultivation in many cases; consider combining mechanical and biological methods when appropriate.
